_note: The hail's beat (O14, 2026-09-29): Bram sees you walk into the ground round the ruined village, a '!' over his head, you are held, he walks over and the conversation opens (Yannick's « dresseur Pokémon »). Where it happens is content/places.json: the points bram_post and brindle_hail, and the hails list, which stays empty until the hail can be seen (O17). The numbers are real seconds at the simulation's own step, so they read the same on both worlds.
_radius_tiles: How far from each of his two points he sees you, in tiles. His ground is two discs side by side across the village's south edge, which every shortest way north from the graves crosses — a long way round can miss it, and then he is found at his post like anyone else — just north of the cemetery and just south of Brindle's heart. Found by search, not by eye (the review of O13-O16 showed a single disc grazed the one walk it was tested on; a bigger one reached into the graves, called you three steps from where you wake and held the talk behind his pines): every shortest walk from where you wake to Brindle's heart and to the bridge crosses it, and so does his trail, while the start, the cemetery and Brindle's heart stay outside — the heart so that a test or a frame standing there is not called out. A fire may stand inside: to wake at one you must have rested there, and to rest there you walked in and were called.
_spotted_seconds: How long the '!' stands over him before he moves: long enough to be read, short enough that the player does not think the game has frozen.
_budget_seconds: How long he has to reach you. A walk that takes longer is a walk that has gone wrong, and the system gives it up rather than hold the player forever.
